why: Every acceptance criterion of RWB-E3-001 to RWB-E3-005 ends with the case in a new state (PROPOSED_IN_COLLINS, WITH_FCR_OFFICER, AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL, AWAITING_SECOND_SIGNATURE, RETURNED_TO_ROUTE_DIL, AFFORDABILITY_IN_ACE), while Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the case and its CMMN state to rwb-case and DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables.

text: The Treatment and TreatmentRequest elements are the DF-TRT fields of TSD S2 T3.1 in camelCase, and treatment is the only table this story creates; the contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements and plan timers get their own tables and field lists with the sibling stories that own them (RWB-S2-E3002 and RWB-S2-E3004). The stage reports its outcome to the parent CaseWorkflow on rwb-case, which owns and moves the case status, so this service writes no case table. The decision code of a treatment event is the rule ID and rule version the evaluated package returned, read as a value in force; no code list is held in code.
why: TSD S2 T-A.2 names the entities without a field list, TSD T3.1 lists the treatment fields only, Architecture v5 slide 41 names four further objects in rwb_treatment with no field list, and no source fixes the decision code of a treatment event.

text: The offer body carries offerAmount, haircutAmount, validityDate, rangeLow, rangeHigh, floor and deviationFlag, and the response carries belowFloor; the range and the floor arrive as facts on the route decision signal from rwb-case, which carries the payoff and range calculated by S1 rwb-valuation (FEAT-VAL-06), and no range, floor or validity column is created in rwb_treatment. The floor in force is the value the signal carries, never a constant.
why: TSD T3.1 has no floor, range or validity column and defines no SettlementOffer entity, the FSD names the range and the floor without naming the fields, and DP-01 forbids copying another service's facts into rwb_treatment.

text: The approval outcome is recorded on the treatment row as approval_level plus the final call, the approver role and the decided-at time, and no new table is created. The delegation level and the limit come from rwb-access's DoA data through the approval request the kit's ApprovalWorkflow carries; rwb-treatment holds no limit of its own. The reason code price_below_floor is a reference value in force. The TreatmentApproved payload carries treatmentId, caseId, treatmentType, offerAmount, approvalLevel, approverRole, finalCall, decidedAt, ruleId and ruleVersion.
why: TSD T3.1 has no second-signature record and no approver reference, the DoA table is rwb-access's under the Ownership Map, no source lists reason codes, and Architecture v5 slide 42 gives TreatmentApproved without a payload.

text: The plan body carries installmentCount, installmentAmount, interestRate, firstDueDate, validUntil, bandLow and bandHigh, and the plan terms are recorded on the treatment row; the band arrives with the ACE affordability result of RWB-S2-E3005 and is recorded with the offer, and no band column is created. text: The calculator is called as one Temporal Nexus operation, calculateRestructurePlan, in the ace-collection namespace, with the case ID, the plan inputs and the rule version in the request, answering affordabilityResult, planRef, installmentAmount, installmentCount and calculatedAt. The result is recorded against the treatment and no affordability or band column is copied from ACE. The call has the 2 s synchronous budget of the one-hop rule and the workflow's retry; when the calculator does not answer the stage stays in AFFORDABILITY_IN_ACE and the caller sees MSG-GEN-006.
why: Architecture v5 slide 18 names the restructure calculator by Nexus only, TSD T5.1 gives INT-34 with no operation, TSD T3.1 has no affordability or plan reference field, and no source states the timeout or the failure answer.
